data.name: Nishat
data.gender_notes: Nishat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nishat is derived from the Urdu word for 'garden' or 'paradise', symbolizing a beautiful and peaceful place. In Islamic tradition, gardens are often associated with paradise and the afterlife. This name conveys a sense of serenity and tranquility. The name Nishat carries the meaning “Garden, Paradise” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Urdu, Persian, Hindi. Parents who choose Nishat usually hope their child will grow to embody garden, paradise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, gardens are a symbol of paradise and the afterlife, reflecting the beauty and tranquility of Allah's creation.
data.etymology: Nishat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Garden, Paradise.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nishat total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: نِشَةَط
in_arabic.long_meaning: نِشَةَط: الحَصاد، المُنتَناه، النَوعِ الأُوَل، وَالنِشَتُ الطَليعَةُ، وَالنَشَطُ المُحَفَّظُ، وَالنِشَطُ المُدَخَّلُ. وَمِنَ الأَسماءِ العُليا، وَالَّتي يُكَرَّمُ الفَضْلُ بِها. وَقِيلَ: نِشَتَهُ الطَليعَةُ وَالنَشَطُ المُحَفَّظُ

in_pashto.name: نِشَت

data.cultural_impact: The name Nishat carries a rich cultural significance as it is derived from the Persian and Urdu word for 'garden' or 'paradise'. Gardens hold a special place in Middle Eastern culture and have been a source of inspiration for poets, artists, and philosophers throughout history. The idea of a lush, beautiful garden represents an escape from the harsh realities of life, offering a place of relaxation, refuge, and renewal. In this context, the name Nishat connotes an aura of elegance, sophistication, and beauty.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, gardens hold profound symbolism in Islamic tradition. They are often used as metaphors for the afterlife, where believers are encouraged to prepare their gardens (i.e., their lives) for the All-Merciful One. In the Quran, Allah says, "The Gardens of Eden are the best of Paradise" (Quran 35:33), indicating the importance and significance of gardens in the hereafter. By carrying this meaning, the name Nishat evokes a connection to the higher spiritual dimensions and serves as an inspiration to lead a virtuous life.
